Tbh.
Can we get our arms down from the sky just a few inches and cut through the hallelujah movement just a bit? Yes AI is massive, Yes AI will change the world. At least for the GPT agent (which I work with on a daily basis)  And see them break and fall and fail again and again to much wasted time and frustration for me and customers and colleagues. comments.author: @FintechFatherAI
comments.text:
MEH... gets a major MEH for me. I suppose for people who cannot code, which is probably most of the population, this will be good. You can make your own langchain agents stuff and get much better results than these. And it would work with things like google docs. But of course, you need to know how to code AND there will be some initial setup of figuring out how to interact with certain things like Google Docs/sheets/etc. using code. If I would have to guess, I'd think that companies similar to how many have made and embraced APIs: companies will start to make AI functions and endpoints which allow users to do things like "cancel auto-recurring orders", etc. 

And then once more of that happens a lot of this stuff falls off the map - I suppose it could be used for a fallback case where that is not available, the user has not programmed a specific tool, etc. That might be good.

But just the results coming out of this... seem UBER MEH at least for now, and for the similar tools I've seen here in the past few months.
